subject: general
question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

“Do you suppose you know better than your own father?” jeered his angry mother.

options.text: His angry mother jeered that did he suppose he knew better than his own father.
His angry mother jeered and asked whether he had supposed he has known better than his own father.
His angry mother jeered and asked if you suppose you know better than your own father.
His angry mother jeered and asked whether he supposed he knew better than his own father.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** “Do you suppose you know better than your own father?” jeered his angry mother.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"Do you suppose" becomes "whether he supposed"**
 
 
• Because it is a Yes/No question, the conjunction "whether" (or "if") is introduced.
 
• The pronoun "you" changes to "he" based on the context of the mother speaking to her son.
 
• The simple present tense verb "suppose" changes to the simple past "supposed".
 
 
 
• **"you know" becomes "he knew"**
 
 
• The simple present "know" shifts backward to the simple past "knew".
 
 
 
• **"your own father" becomes "his own father"**
 
 
• The second-person possessive pronoun "your" changes to the third-person "his".
 
 
 
• **Reporting verb:**
 
 
• The phrase "jeered his angry mother" is structurally adjusted to "His angry mother jeered and asked" to appropriately introduce the indirect question.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *His angry mother jeered and asked whether he supposed he knew better than his own father.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** His angry mother jeered that did he suppose he knew better than his own father.

 
 
• Uses the incorrect conjunction "that" alongside the interrogative form "did he", violating the rules of indirect questions (which must be framed as statements, not questions).
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** His angry mother jeered and asked whether he had supposed he has known better than his own father.
 
 
• Incorrectly changes the tenses to past perfect ("had supposed") and present perfect ("has known") instead of simple past.
 
 
 
• **Option 3:** His angry mother jeered and asked if you suppose you know better than your own father.
 
 
• Fails to convert the pronouns ("you", "your") and the tenses ("suppose", "know") from direct to indirect speech.
